svg.title: An ellipse and Kepler's first law
svg.desc: (a) An ellipse with foci f1 and f2: for any point m on it, the sum of the distances to the two foci is the same, so it can be drawn with a pencil held taut against a loop of string pinned at the foci. (b) A planet of mass m follows an elliptical orbit with the Sun, of mass M, at one focus; r is the distance between their centers. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A taut loop of string draws an ellipse
red: pencil to f₁ · blue: pencil to f₂
The pencil keeps the string taut, so the two distances to the pins always add to the same length.
Planets follow such curves with the Sun at one focus.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
